messages:
Kai: kicking off handoff for the walled-garden customer cluster (on-prem, fully air-gapped). goal: 3 racks, each with 8x A100S 80GB. need final bootstrap runbook + validation checklist and owner assignments. @Marta can you confirm network constraints + egress patterns?

Marta: short version: no outbound internet. customer will provide a jump-gateway in DMZ that we push to. must use their internal registry and NAT gateway for mirror sync. required ports (internal-only): 6443 (k8s api), 2379-2380 (etcd), 10250-10255 (kubelet/probes), 9100 (node exporter), 9103 (nv_gpu exporter), 443 to internal-registry, 123 NTP. We need TCP access between controller plane and GPU nodes on 22, 10250, and 31999-32010 for our debug proxies.

Kai: noted. put a short iptables/ACL snippet we can hand to their network team?

Marta: here's a minimal allowlist they can translate to ACLs (example):

```
# control plane -> nodes
allow tcp any any 22
allow tcp any any 10250
allow tcp apiserver_ip any 6443
# etcd cluster
allow tcp etcd_peer_ips any 2380
allow tcp etcd_client_ips any 2379
# monitoring
allow tcp prometheus_ip any 9100
allow tcp gpu_metrics_ip any 9103
# registry mirror
allow tcp any registry_gateway_ip 443
# ntp/dns
allow udp any ntp_server 123
allow udp any dns_server 53
```

Marta: emphasize: customer firewalls do not allow ICMP, so use tcp-based connectivity checks.

Jen (SRE): air-gapped image flow we used last time: build images in CI, cosign-sign, produce OCI tarball, push to secure staging host, run rsync -> jump-gateway -> import to private registry. commands we used:

```
# build & save
docker build -t registry.local/redwood/inference:1.2.3 .
docker save registry.local/redwood/inference:1.2.3 | gzip > inference-1.2.3.tar.gz
# sign
cosign sign --key cosign.key registry.local/redwood/inference:1.2.3
# import at customer side (after transfer)
ctr -n=k8s.io images import inference-1.2.3.tar.gz
kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml
```

Jen (SRE): ensure imagePullPolicy is IfNotPresent and that nodeImageCache is preloaded. we also add a helm value to prefer localRegistry: true.

ops-bot: artifact-upload: inference-1.2.3.tar.gz uploaded to staging-jump (artifact id: art-6754) :white_check_mark:

Kai: good. validation checklist for cluster health before handoff — draft:
- control plane pods all Running (kube-apiserver, controller-manager, scheduler)
- etcd healthy: `etcdctl endpoint health --cluster` -> OK
- all nodes Ready and GPU drivers reported by daemonset
- nvidia-driver version >= 525 and matching CUDA on runtime images
- run `nvidia-smi -q` on each node -> no ECC errors, correct MIG profiles if used
- run small perf: `./run_infer_bench.sh --model tiny --tokens 256 --iters 10` -> median latency < 120ms on an A100 80GB baseline
- verify GPU metrics exported to Prometheus (gpu_util > 0 during perf run)
- storage: PVCs Bound, throughput tests (fio) show baseline IOPS
- network: iperf3 between control plane and nodes >= expected internal bandwidth -> note baseline: 40Gbps or 100Gbps depending on switch
- security: KMS connection validated (test encryption/decryption), audit logs flowing to their SIEM

Marta: add: firmware mismatch check. customers often have mixed NIC firmware that breaks RDMA. run `ethtool -i` and confirm driver and firmware versions match reference doc.

Jen (SRE): operational run commands for quick checks:
- `kubectl get nodes -o wide`
- `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide`
- `kubectl logs -n infra gpu-daemonset -l app=gpu-driver`
- `ssh jump-gateway 'for n in $(cat nodes); do ssh $n "nvidia-smi -q | grep -E \"Product Name|Driver Version|Ecc Mode\""; done'`

Kai: tests for the inference runtime: deploy a canary service using a tiny open model, run 50 concurrent requests (~batching), verify latency SLOs and KV-cache warmup behavior. check that fallback routing to smaller model works when we artificially saturate the pool.

Amy (CS): on the handoff call with ACME we need: runbook PDF, registry import instructions, firewall allowlist, escalation matrix, and a 1-hr live walkthrough with their infra + security team. Can we get time slots next Tue/Wed?

Kai: propose Tue 16:00 UTC. will send calendar and link. who owns runbook doc?

Jen (SRE): I'll write the operational runbook (short step-by-step) and the validation checklist. ETA EOD Monday.

Marta: I'll polish the network ACL snippet and include the firmware checklist. ETA EOD Monday.

Kai: ops-bot can you create ticket and include artifact id and owners?

ops-bot: ticket created: INFRA-1428 assigned to Jen, Marta; watcher Amy; artifacts: art-6754. Scheduled handoff tentative: 2026-03-24T16:00:00Z.

Kai: last note on cost/ capacity: customer committed to 24 A100S 80GB, but ask them to accept 2 spare hot nodes for rolling updates and failover (adds ~8% spend). recommend we keep 1 node as pre-warmed image cache per rack to avoid long cold-pull times for large weights.

Marta: note on region constraints: their on-prem racks are in different datacenters with limited cross-site bandwidth. we should prefer per-rack model partitions and only replicate small KV caches across sites. document this as constraint in runbook.

Jen (SRE): post-handoff: schedule 48h of elevated monitoring (retain 1s scrape for GPU metrics), alert on GPU driver restarts, OOM kills, high tail latency. we'll hand over Grafana dashboards and alert playbooks.

Amy (CS): all good from CS side. I'll prep customer invite and confirm jump-gateway SSH key exchange process.

Kai: thanks all. action items: Jen (runbook + canary), Marta (network & firmware checklist), Amy (customer invite + paperwork). ops-bot ticket INFRA-1428 tracks this. back here when runbook drafts are ready. :thumbsup:
